subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Sensors: Machines That Feel the World
description: A micro-lesson that makes Sensors: Machines That Feel the World usable.

hook.text: Your phone has at least 14 sensors: accelerometer, gyroscope, magnetometer, barometer, and more.

buildup.text: A sensor converts a physical quantity — temperature, pressure, light — into an electrical signal a circuit can read.

discovery.text: MEMS sensors are microscopic machines etched into silicon. A phone's accelerometer has a tiny mass on a spring.

twist.text: MEMS accelerometers cost under $1 each. In the 1990s, equivalent sensors cost thousands and filled a desktop.

climax.text: IoT devices embed sensors in bridges, factories, and farms. Billions of sensors now feed data to the cloud continuously.

punchline.text: Feel light, heat, motion, pressure. Convert it to numbers. That's sensing.

quiz.question: What are MEMS sensors?
options: Large industrial sensors mounted on factory equipment
Microscopic machines etched into silicon that detect physical quantities
Software algorithms that simulate sensor behavior digitally
